subsystems.name: Feedstock and media preparation
subsystems.role: supplies sugars, nitrogen, vitamins and minerals to the microbes, and sterilises the mixture to prevent contamination.
parts: sugar or starch feedstock (e.g. glucose syrup)

subsystems.name: Bioreactor
subsystems.role: provides a controlled environment where the engineered microbe grows and produces the target protein.
parts: stainless steel vessel (typically 1,000–100,000 litres for pilot to commercial scale)

subsystems.name: Production strain
subsystems.role: the engineered yeast or fungus that makes the protein — for example milk casein, egg white or collagen.
parts: host organism (e.g. Komagataella phaffii, Saccharomyces cerevisiae)
genetic constructs carrying the protein gene
seed train: small flasks to progressively larger seed fermenters

subsystems.name: Downstream processing
subsystems.role: separates the protein from the fermentation broth and purifies it to food grade.

subsystems.name: Utilities and waste handling
subsystems.role: provides energy, water and cooling, and treats waste streams so the plant can sit inside a city.

subsystems.name: Quality control and analytics
subsystems.role: verifies that every batch is safe, consistent and contains the expected protein.

buildSteps.title: Engineer the production strain
buildSteps.detail: Identify the gene for the target protein (e.g. whey, casein, egg white, collagen), insert it into a food-safe yeast or fungus, and screen for strains that secrete large amounts.

buildSteps.title: Design the urban facility
buildSteps.detail: Size the bioreactors (often 10,000–100,000 litres for a demonstration plant), and plan how the site will draw power, water and feedstock from the surrounding city and send waste to treatment.

buildSteps.title: Build the bioreactor and support systems
buildSteps.detail: Fabricate stainless steel vessels, install agitation, aeration, sensors and control software, and connect media preparation and downstream equipment.

buildSteps.title: Prepare and sterilise the media
buildSteps.detail: Mix feedstock with nutrient salts and vitamins, sterilise by heat or filtration, then cool to the fermentation temperature (commonly around 30 °C).

buildSteps.title: Run the fermentation
buildSteps.detail: Inoculate the bioreactor with a growing seed culture, then maintain optimal temperature, pH, oxygen and sugar feed. The microbes multiply and secrete the protein over several days.

buildSteps.title: Harvest and separate
buildSteps.detail: Drain the broth and separate the microbial cells using a centrifuge or microfiltration. The protein of interest is left in the liquid.

buildSteps.title: Purify and dry
buildSteps.detail: Isolate the protein using chromatography or precipitation, then remove water with a spray dryer or freeze dryer to produce a stable powder.

buildSteps.title: Formulate, package and release
buildSteps.detail: Blend the protein with other ingredients to make milk, egg or collagen products, package them, and run quality-control tests before the batch is released for sale.

prerequisites.why: food enzymes such as chymosin have been produced this way since the 1990s, proving the basic method.
antibiotics, amino acids and enzymes are already made in bioreactors of hundreds of cubic metres.
purifying proteins to food safety standards at low cost is still being optimised for many targets.
rules differ by country; some precision-fermentation proteins are approved, others are still under review.

prerequisites.tech: Affordable feedstock and clean energy in cities
prerequisites.why: sugar and agricultural waste are available, but competition for them and for renewable power can limit scale.

pathway.milestone: pilot plants in cities making small batches of milk, egg or collagen proteins for niche foods
pathway.unlocks: proof of concept, early consumer acceptance and operating data.

pathway.milestone: demonstration plants at 100,000-litre scale reaching cost parity for a few proteins
pathway.unlocks: wider adoption by food manufacturers as an ingredient.

pathway.milestone: integration with urban food waste and renewable power as feedstock and energy
pathway.unlocks: a circular production loop that cuts both cost and environmental footprint.

pathway.milestone: a network of urban biorefineries producing staple proteins locally
pathway.unlocks: resilient city food supply with less reliance on animal agriculture and long-distance transport.
